correctness.rationale: The labelled edges with label (f(a,b,c),g(b,c,d)) concatenate an input window by shifting two sites, so a subset transition tracks exactly the possible terminal input states for an aligned output word. All starting and ending input states are allowed. Breadth-first first reach of the empty subset measures shortest forbidden length, and closure without empty proves attainability at every length. Shift-by-two equivariance and compactness then give bi-infinite surjectivity. An independently written exhaustive census gave the complete histogram 708/8552/38436/15920/1776/144 and every cross-tab entry, including 30 homogeneous onto rules, 96 mixed onto pairs and no onto pair with two non-onto constituents. Independent direct windows for (22,105) produce 4,16,64,256,1012 distinct words at lengths 1–5; 10|01|11|11|10 is missing. The reachable subset graph for (51,54) closes without the empty set, while (54,54) loses a length-three word. The source's phrase ‘five-row cross-tabulation’ is descriptive only; the displayed cross-tab correctly has three constituent-count rows.
residual_risks: The first missing aligned pair length can change with phase; the all-pairs theorem can be applied to a swapped order but does not identify its depth with the original order. This is a one-step full-shift result, not a finite-ring or temporal-iterate classification.

value.rationale: Period two is the simplest genuinely nonuniform spatial alternation of the standard elementary rule set. A sharp, practically short ten-bit complete test for bi-infinite surjectivity and a full table of first obstructions are useful exact invariants. The constituent split goes beyond tallying entries: it demonstrates restoration with exactly one non-onto constituent but never two, and shows that two onto constituents do not guarantee onto alternation.
residual_risks: There is no larger-period or radius theorem asserted, and no inference about random or probabilistically mixed cells.
